name: Prague
operatingHours: Metro (lines A, B, C) runs ~4:45 AM–midnight daily, every 2–4 min at peak and 4–10 min otherwise. No all-night metro; night trams and buses run every ~20–30 min from midnight to ~4:30 AM.
fareInfo: One PID ticket covers metro, trams, buses and city ferries with unlimited transfers within its time: 30 min 39 CZK, 90 min 50 CZK (36/46 CZK in the PID Lítačka app; 2026 prices). Day passes: 24 h 150 CZK, 72 h 350 CZK (140/340 in the app). Validate paper tickets on first boarding. The airport trolleybus 59 uses the normal 90-min ticket; the AE Airport Express needs its own ticket.

hotels.name: Augustine, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Prague

sights.name: Old Town Square
sights.note: Prague's medieval main square, framed by Gothic, Baroque and Rococo facades, with the Jan Hus memorial at its centre and Christmas and Easter markets in season.

sights.name: Old Town Hall & Astronomical Clock
sights.note: The 1410 astronomical clock puts on its parade of apostles on the hour; climb or ride the lift up the hall's tower for the best view over the square.
sights.hours: Clock show on the hour ~9 AM–11 PM; tower ~9 AM–9 PM (Mon from ~11 AM)

sights.name: Charles Bridge
sights.note: The 14th-century stone bridge over the Vltava, lined with 30 Baroque statues and Gothic towers at both ends; go at dawn to beat the crowds.

sights.name: Prague Castle
sights.note: One of the largest castle complexes in the world, home to Czech kings and presidents for over a thousand years; the courtyards are free, the historic interiors need a ticket.
sights.hours: Grounds 6 AM–10 PM; historic buildings 9 AM–5 PM (Nov–Mar to 4 PM)

sights.name: St. Vitus Cathedral
sights.note: The Gothic cathedral at the heart of Prague Castle, with a Mucha stained-glass window and the tomb of St. Wenceslas; entry is on the castle ticket.
sights.hours: Mon–Sat 9 AM–5 PM, Sun 12–5 PM (Nov–Mar to 4 PM)

sights.name: Lobkowicz Palace
sights.note: The only privately owned palace inside Prague Castle, showing the Lobkowicz family's art, original Beethoven scores and a café terrace over the city.

sights.name: St. Nicholas Church (Malá Strana)
sights.note: A showpiece of High Baroque with a vast painted dome; the bell tower next door gives a close-up view over Lesser Town's rooftops.

sights.name: Wallenstein Garden
sights.note: A free walled Baroque garden behind the Czech Senate, with a giant arcaded loggia, a dripstone wall and resident peacocks.
sights.hours: Apr–Oct ~7:30 AM–6 PM (weekends from 10 AM, to 7 PM in summer); closed Nov–Mar

sights.name: Petřín Hill & Lookout Tower
sights.note: A wooded hill with orchards, a rose garden and a mini Eiffel Tower from 1891; the funicular from Újezd reopened in September 2026.
sights.hours: Hill open 24h; tower ~10 AM–8 PM (shorter in winter); funicular 7 AM–10:15 PM

sights.name: Jewish Museum (Spanish Synagogue)
sights.note: One ticket covers Josefov's historic synagogues and the Old Jewish Cemetery; the Moorish-style Spanish Synagogue has a stunning gilded interior.
sights.hours: Sun–Fri 9 AM–6 PM (Nov–Mar to 4:30 PM); closed Sat and Jewish holidays

sights.name: Church of Our Lady before Týn
sights.note: The twin black-spired Gothic church that dominates the Old Town Square skyline; astronomer Tycho Brahe is buried inside.
sights.hours: Tue–Sat 10 AM–1 PM & 3–5 PM, Sun 10 AM–12 PM; closed Mon

sights.name: Municipal House
sights.note: Prague's Art Nouveau masterpiece next to the Powder Tower, with Mucha-decorated halls, a concert hall and a grand café downstairs.
sights.hours: Building ~10 AM–8 PM; interiors by guided tour only

sights.name: Head of Franz Kafka
sights.note: David Černý's 11-metre steel head of Kafka outside the Quadrio centre, built from 42 rotating layers that keep breaking apart and realigning.
sights.hours: Outdoors, visible 24h; rotates at intervals through the day

sights.name: Letná Park
sights.note: A plateau above the river with the giant metronome, the classic postcard view of the Vltava's bridges and a popular summer beer garden.

sights.name: Vyšehrad
sights.note: A clifftop fortress south of the centre with the neo-Gothic Basilica of Sts. Peter and Paul, the cemetery where Dvořák and Mucha are buried, and quiet river views.
sights.hours: Grounds open 24h; casemates and basilica ~10 AM–6 PM (shorter in winter)

sights.name: Prague Zoo
sights.note: A large hillside zoo in Troja, rated among the world's best, with a gorilla pavilion, an Indonesian jungle hall and a chairlift; bus 112 from Nádraží Holešovice (metro C).
sights.hours: 9 AM–~4 PM in winter, to ~7 PM in summer

sights.name: Náplavka Farmers' Market
sights.note: A Saturday-morning riverside market on the Vltava embankment with Czech farm produce, street food, local craft beer and wine.

sights.name: Riegrovy sady
sights.note: A hillside park in Vinohrady where locals gather at sunset with a beer from the garden pub, looking across to Prague Castle.
sights.hours: Park open 24h; beer garden ~noon–late in the warmer months

railStations.name: Praha hlavní nádraží
railStations.note: Prague Main Station: EuroCity and railjet trains to Berlin, Dresden, Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest and Kraków, plus national trains to Brno and Ostrava. Metro C stop Hlavní nádraží is underneath; the AE Airport Express bus starts here.
railStations.hours: Station open ~3:15 AM–~12:45 AM. Mainline trains run to individual timetables; metro C ~4:45 AM–midnight.

airports.name: Václav Havel Airport Prague
airports.transitNote: Trolleybus 59 (~17 min) to Nádraží Veleslavín on metro A (shown on map), then ~10 min to Staroměstská/Můstek; an ordinary 90-min PID ticket (46 CZK in app) covers the whole trip. The AE Airport Express bus runs direct to Praha hlavní nádraží in ~35–45 min on a separate fare (~200 CZK). Neither link is rail; the airport is not on the metro map.
airports.hours: Trolleybus 59: first ~4:30 AM, last ~11:30 PM. AE: ~5:30 AM–~10 PM, every 30 min. Late arrivals: night buses 907/910 every ~30 min (0:00–4:30) or a taxi.
